correctness.rationale: For q=2 all admissible noises are the two alternating complement words, so two distinct input words have intersecting output sets iff they are bitwise complements. Thus 2^(n−1) disjoint confusability edges imply M_2(n)=2^(n−1) and exactly 2^(2^(n−1)) maximal transversals. For q≥3, for every input difference d recursively choose z'_(i+1) outside the at most two values z'_i and z'_i+d_i−d_(i+1), and set z_(i+1)=d_(i+1)+z'_(i+1); this realizes any d as two proper-colouring noise differences, making the graph complete. Holds for all n≥1, q≥3 including q=3 boundary. Independent exhaustive difference-set checks covered q=2..5 and n=1..4; symbolic recursion proves the universal statement.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration checks are supplementary; no stochastic noise law, feedback code, or probabilistic capacity assertion.

originality.rationale: The q≥3 impossibility is a quick application of general prior confusability principles after proving specific difference coverage. The finite-block q=2 extremizer classification and 2^(2^(n−1)) labeled optimal codebooks, together with the exact sharp q=2/q≥3 split, are an explicit all-n classification not supplied by the inspected general-capacity references. Priority is best-of-knowledge with low but nonzero risk of an earlier elementary coding lemma.
residual_risks: An earlier elementary treatment of the alternating-binary-noise channel could give the same complete transversals under different language; the count is simple once the complement structure is observed.
The more recent 2021/2022 full article was not fully inspected; no whole-document noncoverage is asserted.

value.rationale: Finite-block zero-error coding for a fixed finite-state adversarial noise constraint is a natural operational invariant, and the q=2-to-q=3 jump from 2^(n−1) reliable messages to one is a sharp alphabet threshold. Counting all 2^(2^(n−1)) maximum binary transversals, not just an asymptotic capacity, provides a fully solved benchmark for exact finite-block code design. The argument is elementary but the exact self-contained all-length classification is motivated by channel confusability, rather than an arbitrary finite slice.
residual_risks: This is a deliberately simple special channel, not a general coding theorem; most of the q≥3 result is implied by existing confusability machinery after a short verification.
